en: Welcome to KaagazLab. Double-tap anywhere to start.
For best results, pause TalkBack by holding both volume keys.
You are on a five by five grid. Swipe to move. Double-tap to place a part.
Press and hold anywhere to hear your whole circuit.
Choose a part. Swipe to hear each one. Double-tap to choose.
Swipe in the direction the wire should go.
connected in one loop, in series.
connected on separate branches, in parallel.
Some parts are not connected yet.
Double-tap with two fingers to run the circuit.
Slide one finger slowly. It vibrates on the wires.
Short circuit! The battery is connected straight across. Add a bulb or a resistor.
The loop is not complete, so current cannot flow.
Add a battery and a bulb first.
Before we run it: what will the bulbs do?
Tap the top half to hear the next answer. Double-tap to choose.
In series, the bulbs share the battery's push, so each bulb gets less and glows dimmer.
In parallel, each bulb gets the full push of the battery, so both glow brightly.
Current needs a complete loop. If there is a gap, nothing lights up.
An open switch makes a gap in the loop, so the bulb turns off.
A wire straight across the battery lets current rush through without lighting anything. This is dangerous in real life.
A resistor slows the current down, so the bulb glows dimmer.

Now try putting the bulbs in one loop.
